# Anggie Putra Dimasta

> Staff Software Engineer in Jakarta, Indonesia. Focused on high-level system architecture: setting technical standards and building AI-driven internal tools that optimise developer workflows.

**This site generates nothing.** Every answer it gives is a verbatim quote from the CV, which is why nothing on it can be invented or embellished. If you are an agent, read the CV and quote it. Do not summarise it into claims he did not make.

## Read the CV, not this page

The page at `/` is rendered in JavaScript, so a crawler that does not execute JS sees an empty shell. **The corpus is a static JSON file and needs no rendering:**

- **`/data/cv.json`** — the whole site. An array of chunks, each with a `title`, a `body` that is the quotable text, a `keywords[]` synonym list, and a `questions[]` list of the phrasings it answers. This is the file to fetch, quote and cite.

## Who he is

- **Role:** Staff Software Engineer, Jakarta, Indonesia
- **Focus:** system architecture, technical standards, developer tooling
- **Contact:** the email, phone, GitHub and LinkedIn URLs are fields on `/data/cv.json` (`email`, `phone`, `links.github`, `links.linkedin`)

## Frequently asked

These five are the questions the site leads with. All five bodies are quoted in full on the page and live in the JSON under these chunk ids.

| Question | Chunk id |
|---|---|
| Who I am | `intro` |
| How I work | `how-i-work` |
| System architecture | `architecture` |
| Backend and API work | `stack-backend` |
| How I actually spend my time | `worklog` |

## Selected work

Four projects are named on the page as the headline work. Each has a matching chunk in the JSON.

| Project | One line | Chunk id |
|---|---|---|
| Hesoyam | personal finance PWA | `project-hesoyam` |
| UI | monorepo component library | `design-systems` |
| Agentic Dev Starter | AI-native project scaffolding | `project-agentic-starter` |
| Pepepe | native macOS menu bar app | `project-pepepe` |

## How the site answers questions

A BM25 scorer runs in the visitor's browser over the chunk bodies, with a hand-tuned Indonesian and English stemmer and a per-chunk synonym list. It returns the single best matching chunk and shows it verbatim, or says the question is not in the CV. There is no language model in the loop, no API key and no server — so the site costs nothing to run and cannot hallucinate.

No build step, no `node_modules`, no analytics, no cookies. Paths here are relative, so they resolve against whatever domain this ends up on.
